card.statement:
Let $\mathbb F$ be a field or
skew field, $V$ be a right
vector space over $\mathbb F$,
and $U$ be its subspace. Let
${\cal A}$ be one of linear
mappings

\begin{equation}
U\rightarrow V,\qquad
V\rightarrow U,\qquad
V/U\rightarrow V,\qquad
V\rightarrow V/U.
\end{equation}

(a) There exists a basis
$e_1,\dots,e_n$ of\/ $V$
satisfying <<ref:m.2>>, in which
for the matrix $A_e$ of ${\cal
A}$ we have:

\[
\begin{cases}
A_e^T,
&\text{if $U\to V$ or $V/U\to
V$,}
\\
A_e, &\text{if $V\to U$ or
$V\to V/U$}
\end{cases}
\]

is a block-direct sum of a
$p$-by-$p$ matrix

\begin{equation}
[K|0_{p0}],\qquad \text{$K$ is
nonsingular,}
\end{equation}

and matrices of the form

\begin{equation}
[J_q(0)|0_{q0}],
\qquad
[J_q(0)|E_q],
\end{equation}

where $E_q$ was defined in
<<ref:bip1s>> $($the summands
<<ref:m.5>> or <<ref:m.6>> may
be absent$)$. The block $K$ is
determined by ${\cal A}$
uniquely up to similarity, and
the summands of the form
<<ref:m.6>> are determined by
${\cal A}$ uniquely up to
permutation.

(b)
If\/ $\mathbb F=\mathbb C$, then
one can replace the summand
<<ref:m.5>> by a block-direct
sum of square matrices of the
form

\begin{equation*}
[J_q(\lambda)|0_{q0}].
\end{equation*}

The obtained matrix is
determined by ${\cal A}$
uniquely up to permutation of
summands, and so it is a
canonical matrix of the linear
mapping ${\cal A}$.
card.label: Theorem 3

paper.title: Classification of sesquilinear forms with the first argument on a subspace or a factor space\footnotetext{This is the authors' version of a work that was published in Linear Algebra Appl. 424 (2007) 282--303.}
paper.abstract: We give canonical matrices of bilinear or sesquilinear forms UxV-->C, (V/U)xV-->C, in which V is a vector space over the field C of complex numbers and U is its subspace.
